mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it predicts a near-term monetary tightening, which reduces discount rates and increases expected equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite FEDFUNDS MA(3) > 4% for the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 160,000 suggests labor market strength, which reduces recession risk and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative when PAYEMS > 160000 for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 102 suggests accelerating business demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO > 102 for ≥ 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 325 indicates supply-side easing, lowering growth expectations and typically producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when CPIAUCSL < 325 for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales (HOUST) above 1200 units signals resilient housing demand, which elevates equity risk premia and yields positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when HOUST > 1200 for ≥ 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.2% indicates labor market tightness that can trigger a Fed rate hike cycle, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when UNRATE < 4.2% for the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) over a month signal supply-side pressures that depress growth expectations and drive negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when both INDPRO and CPIAUCSL are declining for ≥ 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-crisis expansion regime (UNRATE < 4.5% and FEDFUNDS < 5%), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are more likely to be positive due to lower policy uncertainty and stronger growth expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in the specified regime for at least 3 consecutive windows.
